column11: Fabhalta, CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand): $32,520,194.94 over 129 beneficiaries = $252,094.53 per beneficiary a year. It is the only CMS series Fabhalta has - the product was approved for PNH in December 2023 and drug_demand holds no Part B row for it - and it is the figure the dossier prints. For scale, the labelled-year gross is $546,900: the same file gives $32,520,194.94 over 43,408 dosage units = $749.18 a 200 mg capsule, and a labelled year at 200 mg twice daily is 730 capsules (FABHALTA prescribing information, NDA 218276, label effective 2026-07-16, sections 2.2 and 3: '200 mg orally twice daily' in 200 mg capsules)
column12: a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug. $252,094.53 / $546,900 = 0.4610, exactly the share of a labelled year the stopping row below derives from capsules per beneficiary, so the shortfall is counted once rather than twice. The caveat is the sample: 129 Medicare beneficiaries in the product's first full year on the market, when almost every one of them started part-way through it. Both halves of the pair are measured on those same 129 patients, which is what keeps them consistent with each other even though both are launch-year readings

The Kidney Health Initiative's own paediatric IgAN literature review (Pediatr Nephrol 2026, doi:10.1007/s00467-026-07245-2) screened 41 epidemiology articles and cites no US paediatric IgAN rate at all.
